title: What continues
hookLine: three things continue: ongoing charity, useful knowledge, a righteous child's prayer (Muslim)
last: PEACE UPON YOU, PEOPLE OF THE GRAVES.

cards: Three people, all of them gone. One dug a well; nobody drawing water from it now remembers her name, but the water still comes up every morning.
One explained something hard to a student, who explained it to another, until it reached someone who never met him. One raised a child, who now says a parent's name in prayer, alone at night.
Each has died, and the thing they started hasn't stopped. In Islam, a hadith names three things like these.

teach.h: WHEN A PERSON DIES, DEEDS END.
teach.b: Abu Hurayrah reports it, in Sahih Muslim.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said, in paraphrase: when a person dies, their deeds come to an end, except for three. Ongoing charity. Knowledge that people benefit from.
And a righteous child who prays for them. The first sentence is stark. Deeds end.
Whatever a person meant to do tomorrow stays undone. Then the word except, and three doors left open.

Ongoing charity is sadaqah jariyah in Arabic, charity that flows, like running water: not the coin given once, but the thing that keeps giving after the giver is gone, a well, a tree whose fruit people eat, a school, a copy of the Qur'an someone reads from.
The second is knowledge that benefits: not knowledge you merely had, but knowledge passed on and still useful, a recipe, a skill, a way of being kind a student learned by watching you.
The third, a righteous child who prays for you, turns the arrow around. The parent can't do anything more. The child keeps praying, and in the hadith, that still counts for the one who raised them.
What do the three share? Each lives inside other people: the water in someone else's cup, the understanding in someone else's head, the prayer in someone else's mouth.

teach.h: WHAT CONTINUES IS WHAT YOU GAVE.
teach.b: Some readers put it this way: what continues, in this hadith, is what was passed on to someone else.

how: Muslims fund wells, mosques, schools, trees and copies of the Qur'an as sadaqah jariyah, ongoing charity, sometimes in a dead relative's name, citing the hadith in Sahih Muslim on the three things that continue after death.

o: the good name a person leaves, which keeps their memory alive in town
the prayers a person said in life, repeated for them by the angels
charity, useful knowledge and a child's prayer, still counting after death

s: in the hadith, all of a person's deeds keep counting after death
ongoing charity means a gift that keeps giving after the giver dies
sadaqah jariyah: charity that flows, like water.
the hadith's knowledge is any knowledge a person had
it is knowledge that people benefit from.

games.q: you have a sum to give in a parent's memory. which choice fits the hadith's first door best?
o: one nice meal for the family.
a well that keeps giving water.
games.why: ongoing charity keeps giving after the giver is gone; the hadith's word for it describes something that flows.

practice: Let the three come by, one at a time: something that could keep giving after you, something you know that could help someone if you taught it, and the people who might one day remember you in prayer.
Pick just one, and think of the first small step.

wordCard.voice: What continues. The hadith's three: ongoing charity, knowledge that benefits, and a righteous child who prays. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: ongoing charity, charity that keeps flowing.

carryVoice: Your line: three things continue. Each one lives in someone else. That's today, done.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 1631 (when a person dies, deeds end except three)
